subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity — throughput vs latency ops, sizing details
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@lumatek.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai; dylan_brooks@redwood.ai; karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Lumatek inference needs & preferred mode (dedicated)

Hi Laura / team,

Thanks for the call today — great discussion. Per our conversation, Lumatek is leaning toward a Dedicated capacity deployment (reserved GPU pool) because of predictable throughput and data isolation requirements. A few clarifying items we promised to surface so you can put together a preliminary sizing/estimate: 

- Peak TPS (in requests/sec): ~250 (spiky, but sustained bursts of ~60–90s)
- Latency SLO: p95 target ~250ms for generative chat (this is aggressive; happy to trade cost if needed)
- Model family: Llama-2-chat 70B-ish (we're flexible on quantization but want to preserve chat quality)
- Token mix / sequence lengths: mix below (approx): 60% short (8–30 tokens), 30% medium (100–300 tokens), 10% long (800–1,200 tokens)
- Concurrency expectations: typical concurrent sessions ~200 users, peak concurrent model streams ~50, per-request concurrency (kv/cache reuse) TBD
- KV cache usage: session-based chat (moderate reuse, ~1–3 turns average per session)
- Region: prefer us-west for latency to our primary user base
- Compliance: SOC2 + ingress/egress audit logs required; will need guidance on Private (VPC) vs Dedicated tradeoffs for audit visibility

Attachments: I attached a quick traffic snapshot (lumatek_traffic_snapshot_q3.csv) and our high-level requirements doc.

Ask: can you share an early estimate of GPUs we'd want (A100/H100 class?), rough GPU count, expected tokens/sec and token-cost ballpark for Dedicated? Also please advise whether Redwood's Dedicated autoscaling / burst capacity can help with the short 60–90s spikes vs a larger reserved baseline.

Thanks — Samir

Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Lumatek
samir.patel@lumatek.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: lumatek_traffic_snapshot_q3.csv (csv), initial-requirements.pdf (pdf)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai; karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Lumatek inference needs & preferred mode (dedicated)

Samir — thanks for the clear summary and the CSV. This is exactly what we need to start a sizing exercise. High-level takeaways from our side: Dedicated sounds right given your throughput and isolation asks; we have a few knobs to hit the p95 target (batching, KV cache strategy, model variant).

Next steps (proposed):
- Karthik will do a quick throughput modeling pass (GPU candidates + estimated GPUs) based on your CSV + token mix. He may ask for a short sample of full request traces (timestamps + token counts) if available.
- I'll send a pre-filled capacity worksheet (attached) that captures the inputs we need (peak TPS by minute, token length distribution, latency SLO, rollback/fallback policy).
- Quick 30-min follow-up next week to review candidate GPU choices and cost tradeoffs.

For the worksheet I attached (redwood_capacity_worksheet_v1.xlsx) please fill the shaded cells: peak/minute TPS distribution, percent batched requests, and any preferred model quantization options. If you can return by Mon (Nov 2) EOD PST we can have a pre-read ready for the call.

Also: for the p95 250ms target — can you confirm whether that is end-to-end (client-to-client) or model-inference only? That changes the recommendation significantly.

I'll loop in Karthik on the modeling. Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett

laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@lumatek.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Lumatek inference needs & preferred mode (dedicated) — quick modeling questions

Samir / Laura — looping in a few technical clarifications that will materially affect GPU counts and batch behavior. Quick list: 

1) Is the 250 TPS measured at request level (one request => one generation) or at token-level? I.e., do you expect many short requests or fewer multi-token generations?
2) For long requests (800–1,200 tokens), are you streaming partial responses to users or waiting for full generation? Streaming increases concurrency but can hide latency.
3) Do you expect most requests to be cacheable (prefix reuse across sessions) or unique? That drives KV cache benefits.
4) Any strict max batch size we should assume from your app side (some apps have per-request latency ceilings and don't allow large batching).
5) Will you accept an aggressive quantized variant (int8/4) for cost savings if we preserve quality in evals?

Candidate GPUs we'll model: H100 80GB (best throughput for fp16/quant paths), A100 80GB (widely available), and an 48–80GB Ampere flavor for cost tradeoffs. For initial estimates I'll model both a baseline reserved pool + 2x burst nodes (to cover 60–90s spikes) using Redwood Dedicated burst capacity; if you prefer an absolute fixed committed pool we can model that too.

If you can attach a 30–60 minute request-level trace (timestamp + input tokens + output tokens) I can produce a tighter GPU count and GPU-level concurrency recommendation within a day. Otherwise I'll run a conservative estimate from the CSV.

Thanks — Karthik

Karthik Iyer
SVP, Serving & Infra, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@lumatek.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai; dylan_brooks@redwood.ai; Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@lumatek.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Lumatek inference needs & preferred mode (dedicated) — quick modeling questions

Laura / Karthik — quick answers below and I attached a short request-level sample (lumatek_traffic_snapshot_q3.csv):

1) 250 TPS is request-level peak. Most are short bursts (single-turn chat) but about 10% are multi-turn where output tokens can be large.
2) We stream partial responses to clients for UX, so concurrency is higher while per-request wall-clock time increases.
3) Cacheable: ~40% prefix reuse (same user prompts repeated or templated).
4) App-side max batch tolerated: 100ms additional latency budget for batching; otherwise keep batches small in p95-critical paths.
5) Quantization: we are open to int8 if we can validate quality; prefer Redwood's evals before committing.

Concrete numbers we can commit to for modeling:
- Peak request TPS: 250
- Average tokens generated per request: 120 tokens
- Token mix: 60% 8–30, 30% 100–300, 10% 800–1,200
- Target p95 model-inference latency: <= 200ms (we include network + app elsewhere)
- Desired concurrency per GPU target (for planning): ~8 active generations/GPU
- Prefer H100 class if the cost delta is justified; otherwise A100 80GB is acceptable

Please send a preliminary GPU count and a 1–2 slide cost delta summary (H100 vs A100) ahead of the call. We can discuss committed baseline vs burst during the follow-up.

Thanks, Samir

--
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Lumatek
Attachments: lumatek_traffic_snapshot_q3.csv (csv)
